One year of Site Supervisor status experience.

items.item_text: 01. We endeavor to foster a just and inclusive campus culture here at Cuesta College. Please tell us about your experiences with inclusion as it relates to your career or some other aspect of your work? If you have not had direct experience in this area, please tell us about your aspirations. We welcome learning about your areas of challenge or growth and success.
Eligible for the California Child Development Site Supervisor Permit;
Current First Aid and CPR certifications;
Valid driver’s license and eligible to obtain California driver’s license upon hire.

(1) An Associate’s degree from an accredited institution with twenty-four (24) semester units of Early Childhood Education/Child Development including the following core courses of child/human growth and development; child, family, and community or child and family relations; and programs/curriculum; AND completion of six (6) additional semester units of course work in the administration and supervision of childcare and development programs; AND completion of two (2) semester units of adult supervision course work; AND an additional two (2) years’ experience.

(2) A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with twenty-four (24) semester units of Early Childhood Education/Child Development including the following core courses of child/human growth and development; child, family, and community or child and family relations; and programs/curriculum; AND completion of six (6) additional semester units of course work in the administration and supervision of childcare and development programs; AND completion of two (2) semester units of adult supervision course work.
Experience
One year of Site Supervisor status experience.
A minimum of two years’ experience working in an early childhood or children’s program learning environment serving children under five years of age.
Experience
Provide day-to-day leadership and oversite of the assigned Children’s Center site;
Plan, organize, manage, integrate and evaluate the work of staff;
Participate in developing program philosophy, goals and objectives in collaboration with faculty and staff;
Monitor compliance and coordinate implementation of all licensing regulations (Title XXII) pertaining to daily operational needs of the Center;
Recommend and assist with budget management;
Assist with record keeping and reporting;
Assist in the written assessment and evaluation of children’s growth and development;
Facilitate positive interpersonal relations with parents by participating in parent conferences as needed or requested, daily parent communication, and parent meetings;
Follow procedures for child abuse reporting as required by law;
Assist with the recruitment of staff, process monthly time cards and leaves;
Maintain health and safety standards including nutritional programs, universal health precautions, emergency procedures, and facility and equipment safety for children, parents, staff and students;
Advise and assist site staff in the resolution of work-related problems;
Assist laboratory students in their assignments;
Demonstrate a sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students;
Maintain files for children attending the Center and for licensing purposes;
Collaborate with Director on children’s center policies;
Enroll children, conduct parent tours and orientations, and maintain waitlists; and
Perform other related duties as required.
As a substitute until the permanent position is filled, the job duties may be a subset of the below essential functions.
Education
(2 options) – Individuals must satisfy all the requirements listed in one of the following options:
Child development, health, and nutritional guidelines and theories of child guidance;
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with those contacted in the performance of duties; and
Family relationships;
See for the purpose of reading regulations, laws and codes, rules and policies, and other printed matter;
Methods of record keeping and reporting;
Hear and understand speech at normal levels;
Health and safety regulations;
Speak so that others will be able to understand a normal in-person and telephone conversation;
Both program specific and District operational policies and procedures;
Sit or stand for extended periods of time both indoors and outdoors;
Current technologies, personal computer, and associated office software such as word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, and/or database software;
Lift and/or carry 50 pounds;
Correct English usage: grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation;
Bend and twist, push and pull, stoop, kneel;
Current technologies, personal computer, and associated office software such as word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, and/or database software; and
Reach in all directions;
Correct usage of English, grammar, spelling, punctuation, and vocabulary.
Sit on floor and/or at small tables and chairs; and
Exert manual dexterity sufficient for keyboard and other office equipment operation.
Up to date immunization records including MMR and DTP;
How to communicate effectively with preschool age children and their parents;

Demonstrate a sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students. "Meaningful consideration" means that candidates shall be required to demonstrate sensitivity to diversity in ways relevant to the specific position.
